title: Beef Wellington
description: Seared tenderloin wrapped in mushroom duxelles, prosciutto and puff pastry.
ingredients: 1 beef tenderloin center cut (2 1/2 lb), trimmed
steps: Tie the tenderloin at intervals so it holds a round shape, season heavily, and sear it in the oil over very high heat for 60 seconds on every surface until uniformly browned. Cool completely, then untie and brush all over with Dijon.

Pulse the mushrooms and garlic to a fine crumb and fry in the butter over high heat 15-20 minutes until all the water has gone and the duxelles is a dry, dark paste. Add the sherry and thyme and cook it off. Wet duxelles is the single most common cause of soggy Wellington - keep going until the pan is dry.
Lay the prosciutto out in an overlapping rectangle on plastic wrap, spread the cooled duxelles over it, set the beef on top and use the wrap to roll it into a tight cylinder. Chill 30 minutes.
Roll the puff pastry, unwrap the beef parcel onto it and roll up, sealing the seam and ends. Chill another 30 minutes seam-side down.
Brush with egg yolk, score the top lightly, scatter flaky salt and bake at 400F for 35-40 minutes to 125F internal for medium-rare.
Rest a full 15 minutes before slicing thick with a serrated knife.

title: Soft Scrambled Eggs
description: Eggs cooked on and off the heat into small, custardy curds with creme fraiche.
steps: Crack the eggs straight into a cold saucepan with the butter. Do not beat them first and do not season yet - salt added early draws out water and makes them weep.
Set the pan over medium heat and stir continuously with a rubber spatula, scraping the base and sides.

After about 30 seconds, lift the pan off the heat for 20 seconds while still stirring, then return it. Keep alternating on and off. This is the whole technique: the eggs set gently in small curds instead of seizing into rubber.
After 4-5 minutes of this they will thicken into a glossy, loose custard. Pull them while they still look slightly underdone - they keep cooking from residual heat.
Stir in the creme fraiche off the heat to stop the cooking dead, then season with salt and pepper.
Pile onto toast and finish with chives.

title: Pan-Roasted Sirloin with Thyme Butter
description: A hard sear, then constant basting in foaming garlic-thyme butter.
steps: Salt the steaks and leave them uncovered on a rack at room temperature 30 minutes, then pat the surface bone dry and add the pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan until it just smokes. Lay the steaks in away from you and leave them untouched for 3 minutes.
Flip, then stand each steak on its fat edge for 60 seconds to render it - that strip of fat carries most of the flavor.
Lay them flat, add the butter, garlic and thyme, and tilt the pan so the butter pools. Spoon it over the steaks continuously for 2-3 minutes.
Pull at 125F for medium-rare, using a thermometer rather than timing.
Rest 8 minutes on a board, then slice against the grain and pour the resting juices and pan butter back over.

title: Sticky Toffee Pudding
description: Date sponge drenched in hot toffee sauce. Britain's best pudding.
ingredients: 1 cup dark brown sugar, for the sauce
steps: Pour the boiling water over the chopped dates, stir in the baking soda and leave 15 minutes. The soda breaks the dates down into the pulp that gives the sponge its dark, sticky crumb.
Cream the butter and brown sugar 3 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time and the vanilla.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt, then the date mixture with all its liquid. The batter will look alarmingly loose - that is correct.
Pour into a buttered 9x9 pan and bake at 350F for 35-40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Meanwhile simmer the sauce ingredients together 5-6 minutes until it thickens and coats a spoon. Add the rum and flaky salt at the end.
Prick the hot sponge all over with a skewer and pour a third of the sauce over so it soaks in. Serve warm with the rest of the sauce and cream.

title: Shepherd's Pie
description: Lamb braised with Worcestershire and thyme under a piped potato crust.
steps: Brown the lamb hard in the oil over high heat, in batches so it colors rather than steams, then drain off the fat.
Cook the onions and carrots 8 minutes, add the garlic and tomato paste for 2 minutes, then the Worcestershire and wine. Reduce by half.
Add the broth and thyme and simmer 25 minutes until thick enough that a spoon leaves a clean trail. Season and spread in a baking dish.
Boil the potatoes until tender, drain and leave them in the dry pan over low heat 1 minute to steam off moisture.
Mash with the butter and warm milk, then beat in the egg yolks and half the Parmesan. The yolks are what let the topping brown and hold its shape when piped.
Pipe or spread the mash over the filling, seal it to the edges, rough up the surface, scatter the rest of the Parmesan and bake at 400F for 25-30 minutes until deep golden.

title: Beer-Battered Fish and Chips
description: Cod in a crisp beer batter with twice-fried chips and mushy peas.
ingredients: 2 1/2 lb russet potatoes, cut in thick chips
steps: Rinse the cut chips, then fry them at 275F for 8 minutes until tender but pale. Lift out and cool. This first low fry cooks the inside; the second makes the shell.

Whisk the flour, cornstarch, baking powder and salt, then pour in the cold lager and whisk only until just combined. Lumps are fine. Cold, barely-mixed batter fries lightest, so make it at the last moment.
Raise the oil to 375F and fry the chips again for 3-4 minutes until deep golden. Drain on a rack and salt at once.
Pat the cod completely dry and dust it lightly in plain flour so the batter grips.
Lower the oil to 350F. Dip each fillet, let the excess run off, and lower it in, holding it for 5 seconds before releasing so it does not stick. Fry 6-7 minutes until the batter is golden and rigid.
Crush the cooked peas roughly with the butter, mint and salt. Serve everything with lemon and tartar sauce.

title: Lobster Ravioli
description: Hand-rolled pasta filled with lobster and scallop mousse in a shellfish bisque.
ingredients: 2 cooked lobster tails, meat chopped, shells reserved
1/2 cup heavy cream, for the sauce
steps: Make the pasta: mix the flour, eggs, yolks and salt, knead 10 minutes until smooth and springy, then wrap and rest 1 hour. Skipping the rest makes the dough fight you when rolling.
Blitz the scallops with the 1/4 cup cream to a smooth mousse, then fold in the chopped lobster, chives and lemon zest. Chill.

Make the bisque: fry the reserved shells in the butter 5 minutes, add the shallot, fennel and tomato paste for 3 minutes, flame off the brandy, then add the wine and broth. Simmer 30 minutes, strain hard through a sieve pressing the shells, then reduce by half and finish with the cream and cayenne.
Roll the pasta down to the thinnest setting - you should be able to read through it. Work with one sheet at a time and keep the rest covered.

Place teaspoons of filling along the sheet, brush around each with egg, lay a second sheet over and press out every bit of air from the center outwards before cutting. Trapped air bursts the ravioli in the water.
Poach the ravioli in barely simmering salted water 3-4 minutes, lift out with a slotted spoon and serve in shallow bowls with the hot bisque poured around.

title: Pan-Fried Sea Bass with Crushed Potatoes
description: Crisp-skinned bass over lemon-crushed new potatoes.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, 18 minutes, then drain and crush them roughly with a fork - flattened but not mashed.
Fold in 2 tbsp butter, the capers, lemon juice, zest and herbs, and season. Keep warm.

Score the fish skin three times per fillet and pat it bone dry. Season the skin heavily with salt only at the moment it goes in the pan; salt sitting on it draws out moisture and you lose the crispness.
Heat the oil until it shimmers and lay the fillets in skin-side down. Press each one flat with a spatula for 20 seconds so the skin does not curl away from the pan.
Cook 4-5 minutes without moving them - you will see the flesh turn opaque from the bottom up through about three quarters of its thickness.
Flip, add the remaining butter and garlic, baste for 30-45 seconds and serve skin-side up on the crushed potatoes.

title: Red Wine Braised Short Ribs
description: Short ribs braised in red wine until the sauce turns glossy.
steps: Season the ribs heavily and dust with flour. Brown them in the oil on every side, in batches, 12 minutes total. Do not rush this - the crust is the backbone of the sauce.
Cook the onions, carrots and celery in the same pot 10 minutes, then the garlic and tomato paste for 3 minutes until the paste darkens to brick.
Pour in the wine, scrape the bottom clean and reduce it by half, about 12 minutes. Reducing the wine properly removes the raw, sharp edge.
Return the ribs, add the broth, thyme and bay leaves so the liquid comes two thirds up the meat, cover and braise at 325F for 3 hours.
Lift the ribs out, strain the liquid and skim off the fat, then reduce it on the stove until it coats a spoon. Whisk in the butter off the heat for gloss.
Return the ribs to the sauce to glaze and serve over mash or polenta.

title: Scotch Eggs
description: Soft-boiled eggs wrapped in sausage, breaded and fried.
steps: Lower 6 eggs into boiling water for exactly 6 minutes, then plunge them into ice water and peel very carefully. Six minutes gives a set white and a molten yolk, which is the point of a good Scotch egg.
Mix the sausage meat with the herbs, mustard powder, salt and pepper and divide into 6 portions.
Flatten each portion between sheets of plastic into a disc, set a peeled egg in the middle and bring the meat up around it, sealing with wet hands so there are no gaps.
Beat the last egg. Roll each ball in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing it on firmly.
Fry in 325F oil for 8-9 minutes, turning, until deep golden and the sausage is cooked through. Any hotter and the crust burns before the meat is done.
Drain on a rack, rest 5 minutes and serve warm, halved, with English mustard.

title: Herb-Crusted Rack of Lamb
description: Rack of lamb seared, painted with mustard and pressed in a herb crumb.
ingredients: 2 racks of lamb (8 bones each), trimmed
steps: Blitz the panko, parsley, rosemary, thyme, garlic and Parmesan into a bright green crumb, then stir in the melted butter so it clumps slightly.
Season the racks and sear them hard in the oil, fat-side down first, 2-3 minutes per side until well browned. Let them cool for 5 minutes.
Brush all over with Dijon - it is the glue as much as the seasoning.
Press the herb crumb firmly onto the fat side in a thick even layer.
Roast at 400F for 18-22 minutes to 128F internal for medium-rare. Tent the crust loosely with foil if it browns before the lamb is ready.
Rest 10 minutes - non-negotiable here - then carve into double chops between the bones.

title: Chicken Supreme with Mushroom Sauce
description: Skin-on chicken breast roasted hard and finished in a cream mushroom sauce.
steps: Pat the chicken dry and season. Lay it skin-side down in the oil in a cold oven-safe pan, then bring the heat up to medium-high. Starting cold renders the fat out slowly and gives you genuinely crisp skin.
Cook 8-10 minutes without moving it, until the skin is deep golden and releases on its own.
Add 2 tbsp butter, the thyme and garlic, baste the chicken, then transfer the pan to a 400F oven for 12-15 minutes to 160F internal. Rest the chicken skin-side up on a board.
Pour off the fat, add the remaining butter and cook the shallots 3 minutes, then the mushrooms over high heat 6 minutes until browned and dry.
Add the wine and reduce by half, then the broth and reduce by half again, scraping the pan.
Stir in the cream and simmer 3 minutes until it coats a spoon. Add the tarragon and any resting juices, and spoon the sauce around - not over - the crisp skin.

title: Full English Breakfast
description: Sausages, bacon, eggs, beans, tomato and mushrooms, all timed to land together.
steps: Start the sausages first since they take longest: brown them in a little oil over medium heat, turning often, for 15-18 minutes. Move them to a low oven to hold.
Cook the bacon in the same pan until crisp, then hold it in the oven too. The rendered fat from both is your cooking medium for everything else.
Fry the mushrooms over high heat 5 minutes until browned, then the tomatoes cut-side down 4 minutes until they slump and char. Season both.
Warm the beans in a small pan. Toast the bread.
Fry the eggs last, in butter over medium heat, 2-3 minutes, spooning butter over the whites so they set while the yolks stay runny.
Plate everything at once. A full English is really an exercise in sequencing - cook it in the order above and nothing goes cold.

title: Mushroom Risotto
description: Risotto built in stages with porcini stock and finished off the heat.
steps: Soak the porcini in a cup of the hot broth for 20 minutes, then chop them and strain the soaking liquid back into the rest of the broth. That liquid is the most concentrated mushroom flavor in the dish.
Sear the fresh mushrooms in the olive oil over high heat, undisturbed 4 minutes before stirring, until well browned. Season and set aside.
Sweat the shallots in 2 tbsp butter 4 minutes without coloring, add the garlic, then the rice and toast 2 minutes until the grains are translucent at the edges.

Add the wine and stir until absorbed. Then add the hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting for each to be nearly absorbed. This takes 18 minutes and the stirring is what releases the starch.
Fold in the chopped porcini and three quarters of the seared mushrooms in the last 5 minutes.
Off the heat, beat in the remaining butter and the Parmesan hard until the risotto ripples when you shake the pan. Top with the reserved mushrooms, thyme, parsley and a few drops of truffle oil.

title: Crispy Pork Belly
description: Slow-roasted belly finished at high heat for blistered crackling.
steps: Score the skin in fine parallel lines 1/4 inch apart, cutting through the skin but not into the meat. Pat it absolutely dry.
Toast and crush the fennel seeds and peppercorns, mix with the garlic, rosemary and pepper flakes, and rub this into the meat side only. Rub the skin with the kosher salt alone.
Refrigerate uncovered, skin-side up, for at least 12 hours. This drying step is the whole difference between crackling and leather, and nothing substitutes for it.
Wipe the salt off the skin and pat dry again. Set the belly on the onions and apples in a roasting pan and pour the cider and broth around, keeping the skin dry and above the liquid.
Roast at 300F for 3 hours until the meat is completely tender.
Raise the oven to 475F and roast 25-35 minutes more, watching closely, until the skin puffs and blisters all over. Rest 20 minutes, then cut through the crackling with a serrated knife.

title: Beef Stroganoff
description: Quick-seared strips of beef in a mustard, paprika and sour cream sauce.
ingredients: 2 lb beef sirloin, cut in thin strips
steps: Pat the beef strips very dry and season. Sear them in the oil over the highest heat in two batches, 60-90 seconds each, just to brown the outside. Take them out while still rare - they finish in the sauce, and any longer here means tough beef.
Add the butter and cook the shallots 3 minutes, then the mushrooms over high heat 6 minutes until browned.
Add the garlic, Dijon and smoked paprika and cook 1 minute.
Take the pan off the heat before adding the brandy, then return it and reduce by half.
Add the broth and simmer 5 minutes to reduce slightly, then lower the heat right down and stir in the sour cream. It must not boil after this or it will split.
Return the beef and its juices for 1 minute, add the dill and serve over egg noodles.

title: Chocolate Fondant
description: Individual chocolate cakes with liquid centers. Timing is everything.
ingredients: 3 tbsp butter, softened, for the molds
3 tbsp cocoa powder, for the molds
steps: Prepare the molds properly or nothing else matters: brush 6 ramekins with softened butter in upward strokes, chill them 10 minutes, butter again, then dust with cocoa and tap out the excess.
Melt the chocolate and butter together over barely simmering water, then cool 10 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, yolks and sugar for 4-5 minutes until pale, thick and tripled in volume. This aeration is what lifts the cake around the molten center.
Fold the chocolate into the eggs, then sift in the flour and salt and fold until just combined.
Divide between the molds and chill at least 30 minutes. Chilled batter buys you a wider margin on the bake.

Bake at 400F for exactly 12 minutes - the tops should be set with a slight wobble in the middle. Rest 1 minute, run a knife around each, invert onto plates and serve immediately with ice cream. A minute too long and you have cake instead of fondant.

title: Eton Mess
description: Crushed meringue, whipped cream and macerated strawberries, folded loosely.
ingredients: 1/4 cup powdered sugar, for the cream
steps: Halve two thirds of the strawberries and toss them with the 1/3 cup powdered sugar, lemon juice and balsamic. Leave 30 minutes until they release their juices - the balsamic sounds odd and makes the fruit taste more like itself.
Blitz or mash the remaining third into a rough puree.
Whip the cream with the 1/4 cup powdered sugar and vanilla to soft peaks only. Stiff cream makes a stodgy mess; it should just hold a floppy peak.
Break the meringues into large shards with your hands.
Fold the cream, puree, macerated berries and most of the meringue together with two or three strokes only. The point is streaks, not a uniform pink mixture.
Spoon into glasses, top with the remaining meringue and mint, and serve within 20 minutes before the meringue dissolves.

title: Pan-Roasted Chicken with Sage Butter
description: Chicken breast with crisp skin, basted in sage and garlic butter.
steps: Pat the chicken completely dry and season both sides. Dry skin is the only route to crisp skin.
Lay the breasts skin-side down in the oil in a cold pan, then turn the heat to medium. Press them flat with a spatula for the first 30 seconds so the whole surface contacts the pan.
Cook 10-12 minutes without touching them, until the skin is deep golden and lifts away cleanly.
Flip, add the butter, sage and garlic, and cook 6-8 minutes more, tilting the pan and spooning the foaming butter over continuously.
Pull at 160F internal and squeeze the lemon into the pan.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice and pour the sage butter and pan juices over, finishing with parsley.

title: Seared Scallops with Pea Puree
description: Caramelized scallops over bright mint pea puree with crisp pancetta.
steps: Buy dry-packed scallops if you can. Wet-packed ones are treated with phosphate solution, release water in the pan and will never brown.
Crisp the pancetta in a dry pan, then lift it out, leaving the fat.
Simmer the peas in the broth 4 minutes, then blend with the cream, mint, lemon juice and salt until completely smooth. Push it through a sieve for a restaurant texture. Keep warm.
Pat the scallops bone dry on paper towels and season just before cooking.
Heat the oil in the pancetta pan until it just smokes. Lay the scallops in with space between them and do not touch them for 90 seconds - crowding drops the temperature and they steam.
Flip, add the butter and baste for 45-60 seconds. They should be golden outside and barely opaque in the middle. Serve on the puree with the pancetta and chives.

title: The Ultimate Burger
description: A thick chuck-and-brisket patty with caramelized onions and garlic aioli.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb ground chuck and brisket blend (80/20)
steps: Cook the onions in the butter over medium-low for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until jammy and deep brown. There is no shortcut; high heat gives you burnt edges and raw centers.
Stir the mayonnaise with the garlic, Dijon and lemon juice for the aioli.
Form 4 loose patties slightly wider than the buns and press a dimple in each center so they do not dome. Handle the meat as little as possible - compacted patties cook dense.
Season both sides only as they go into the pan. Sear in the oil over high heat 3-4 minutes per side for medium.
Add the cheddar after the flip and cover for 1 minute to melt.
Toast the buns in the pan, spread both halves with aioli, and build with lettuce, the patty, onions and tomato. Rest the burger 2 minutes before eating so the juices settle.

title: Roasted Tomato Soup
description: Tomatoes roasted hard with garlic and thyme, then blended with basil.
steps: Toss the tomatoes, peppers, onions and unpeeled garlic with the oil, salt, pepper, pepper flakes, thyme and sugar on two sheet pans, tomatoes cut-side up.
Roast at 425F for 45 minutes until everything is collapsed and charred at the edges. Those blackened patches are the whole point - pale roasted vegetables make a thin soup.
Squeeze the garlic out of its skins and discard the thyme stems.
Blend everything with the broth and basil until smooth, working in batches and venting the lid.
Pour into a pot, bring to a simmer and stir in the cream and balsamic.
Taste and adjust - roasted tomatoes vary enormously, so it may want more salt, sugar or vinegar.

title: Sunday Roast Beef with Yorkshire Puddings
description: Rib roast with gravy and Yorkshire puddings risen in smoking beef fat.
ingredients: 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, for the gravy
steps: Make the Yorkshire batter first: whisk the flour, eggs, milk and salt until smooth and rest it at room temperature at least 1 hour. Rested batter rises far higher.
Bring the beef to room temperature, pat dry, rub with mustard, oil, salt and pepper and press the thyme on. Set it on the onions and carrots in a roasting pan.
Roast at 450F for 20 minutes, then drop to 325F for about 1 1/4 hours, to 125F internal for medium-rare.
Move the beef to a board to rest at least 25 minutes, loosely covered. Pour the drippings into a muffin tin, dividing them between 12 cups.

Raise the oven to 450F and heat the tin until the fat is actually smoking, then pour in the batter and bake 20-22 minutes without opening the door. Smoking fat and an unopened door are the two rules of Yorkshire puddings.
Make the gravy in the roasting pan: stir the flour into the remaining juices, add the wine and reduce, then the broth, and simmer until it coats a spoon. Strain and serve with the carved beef.

title: Crispy Salmon with Lemon Butter
description: Salmon cooked almost entirely skin-side down until the skin shatters.
ingredients: 4 salmon fillets, skin on (6 oz each)
steps: Pat the salmon skin bone dry and score it twice per fillet. Season it right before cooking.
Heat the oil in a pan until it shimmers, then lay the fillets in skin-side down, pressing each flat for 15 seconds so the skin stays in full contact.

Cook 6-8 minutes on the skin alone. You will see the flesh turn opaque from the bottom up - wait until it has changed about three quarters of the way through. Roughly 80 percent of the cooking happens on this side.
Flip and cook only 60-90 seconds on the flesh side.
Add the butter, garlic and thyme and baste for 30 seconds.
Take the pan off the heat, add the lemon juice, zest and capers, and spoon the sauce around the fish so the skin stays crisp. Finish with chives.

title: Bread and Butter Pudding
description: Buttered brioche soaked in vanilla custard and baked until the top crisps.
steps: Soak the raisins in the rum while you work.
Butter the brioche slices generously on one side and cut them into triangles. Use day-old bread - fresh brioche collapses into mush.

Warm the milk, cream and scraped vanilla bean until steaming but not boiling. Whisk the eggs, sugar and salt, then pour the hot cream in slowly while whisking so the eggs do not scramble. Strain the custard.
Layer the brioche in a buttered dish, butter side up and overlapping, scattering the drained raisins between layers.
Pour the custard over and press the bread down gently. Leave it 20 minutes to soak - this is what makes the inside custardy rather than dry.
Scatter the demerara sugar over and bake at 350F for 45-50 minutes until puffed and golden with a crisp top and a slight wobble. Brush with warmed apricot jam and serve warm.
